In my opinion, the drugs are not helping. I don't know your full story and am basing what I think off of what you've told is, but I really think the depression medications are no good for your stability. You've been subjected to some pretty terrible experiences and the meds are just numbing you to it all. Let alone every time you take those pills your reminded of these terrible things that happened that are making you take the pills. You should take some time away from men and focus on what makes you happy. Do something that you would consider brave. Prove to yourself that you can do things your medications say you can't. It sounds like you've fallen victim to a lot of things in your life and it's your turn to be an aggressor. Not in a negative way though. Positive aggression is a great way to feel good about yourself. Go to an animal shelter and give some time to help walk the dogs. Go to a children's hospital and color and draw with the kids. Join a local group that actively does good for your area. Put yourself in a situation where you're a positive influence on a victim. It'll help you see that you're not the only one suffering through awful things. As for dating I'd recommend getting set up with someone through a friend or co-worker you trust. Be upfront with the new guy. Maybe even request that he be tied up in bed so you can feel a sense of security while being with him for the first few times. It's not fair that you've dealt with assholes thus far, but it's important to know that there are men out there that are capable of loving you for your scars and would never do anything to hurt you. Don't sell yourself short. You seem like a good person who's been taken advantage of too many times. Don't let the negativity run your life. Take it and use it a fuel to do good for others. You'll gain a whole new circle of friends that hold you in high regards and it'll in turn make you feel more fulfilled.

I've had similar thoughts but have always encountered two stumbling blocks: the courage to do it, and the lasting effects.  While the lack of courage stops me first, the thought of the lasting effects would probably stop me second, should I muster the courage.  In my opinion, human existence is pointless, a mundane exercise.  However, some people important to me, namely my friends and family, have found a reason to exist, and they actually seem genuinely happy.  Why wreck their happiness just because I'm in pain?  Regardless of how pointless I think life is, they have happiness.  To kill myself would shatter their worlds, or at least fracture them permanently.  I know that it would cause irreparable pain to my mother and my grandparents.  Personally, I'd rather have a legacy of personal sadness and misery than one of distributed pain.

I've always thought this. Depression goes so much deeper than just emotional pain. It affects every single tiny aspect of your life, of your existence. It changes who you are. Even though society has come quite far in terms of recognizing mental illness as a true affliction, I feel as though there is still a stigma attached to depression. People like us are typically seen as lazy, slovenly, cold, etc, because our condition is just so hard to relate to. Sure, the average person has bad days and experiences 'the blues', but I think most of our peers are frightened at the idea of an existence completely lacking in joy and purpose. They can't relate to it. When I hear people talk, its always about things happening in their life - their future plans, exciting news, dreams and aspirations, even their passions and frustrations. I think this is why so many of us feel the need to wear a mask - if our peers knew that all we care to discuss is our neverending misery, our hopelessness, our desire to leave this life.. it would terrify and possibly disgust them.

I guess my point is, the bulk of society does not understand our affliction. Thus, they cannot appreciate the need for people in our position to make that final call. I hope countries like the USA will one day adopt policies to make this possible. It's an option I've pined for many times over.

The doctor pushes you into any sketchy inpatient program that has room for you so they won't be liable if you try again.  If you try to assert your own rights as an individual and refuse an inpatient therapy program (you know, as an ADULT CITIZEN) you know nothing about they most likely will threaten to get the courts involved.  The place I was sent through did intake sessions via skype with the door open, fully in earshot of an entire lobby of people herded there from the same hospital I was referred from.  So many HIPAA violations I could hardly count them all.

If there is even a tiny part of you that wants to keep on going, don't do it.  Because the moment you try to hurt yourself and get caught.... TRUST ME, your life will NOT be in your own hands anymore.
